candidate.claim: Fixed-window zeta maxima distinguish the three-halves centering and predicted density, while partition-function free energy tests the beta=1 freezing plateau directly.
candidate.proposed_limit: Slow convergence, lower-order arithmetic corrections, and two-column extraction prevent the reported agreement from being conclusive.
candidate.title: Two numerical observables test different parts of the freezing picture

parents.context_note: This is empirical support for a model choice, not a theorem about zeta extremes.
parents.representation_dependency: Two-column extraction interleaves equations from the CUE derivation; the data protocol, alternatives, and conclusion are explicit.
parents.selection_reason: Describes the fixed-length zeta computation and compares the observed mean with the c=3/2 log-correlated prediction and the c=1/2 short-range prediction, finding the former substantially closer.
parents.title: The mean maximum favors the log-correlated three-halves correction

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The observed mean local maximum discriminates between two lower-order extreme-value corrections: the log-correlated c=3/2 normalization stays much nearer one than the short-range c=1/2 normalization.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: It recognizes the lower-order correction, rather than leading growth alone, as the statistic capable of separating the candidate correlation classes.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted as criticized: the concrete statistic, N approximately log T dependence, sampling design, and numerical epistemic limit are all preserved despite column interleaving.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The computation samples zeta on length-2pi intervals at several heights, sets N to the nearest integer to log T, and reports tabulated mean ratios under the two competing corrections.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: This is finite-height, protocol-dependent numerical support for a model, not proof of a zeta extreme-value law.

parents.context_note: Overlaps the immutable prediction unit because the source prints theory and evidence in parallel columns.
parents.representation_dependency: The page layout interleaves theory and experiment, but the caveat and tail discussion are prose-recoverable.
parents.selection_reason: Compares the normalized zeta-maximum distribution with the predicted density, emphasizes slow convergence and omitted lower-order arithmetic terms, and rejects treating the agreement as conclusive.
parents.title: Distributional zeta numerics are supportive but slow and arithmetically incomplete

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The centered maximum distribution and its left tail separate a proposed universal log-correlated signature from short-range Gumbel behavior, while slow convergence and omitted arithmetic corrections limit what the numerical match can establish.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: It uses tail shape and convergence rate to distinguish a limiting universality claim from arithmetic finite-height effects and preserves the source's warning about large-deviation extrapolation.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted as criticized: no numerical agreement is promoted to verification, and the figure-normalization and lower-order-renormalization dependencies remain visible.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span gives the CUE-centered law, Bessel density and left tail, contrasts it with the Gumbel tail, and compares normalized zeta maxima near height 10^28 while explicitly calling the agreement supportive but inconclusive.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Universality and persistence of the observed tail are heuristic; the source itself calls the large-deviation implication unlikely and the present evidence nonconclusive.

parents.context_note: The exact span necessarily contains figure coordinates and interleaved references because of two-column extraction; the definition at lines 261-269 and result at lines 339-347 are both readable.
parents.representation_dependency: Strong layout dependency; use the original PDF for the plotted data and exact lower-order renormalization, while the qualitative freezing test is explicit in prose.
parents.selection_reason: Defines the fixed-window zeta analogue of the partition function and reports that its normalized free energy follows beta+1/beta below beta=1 and remains near 2 above it.
parents.title: The zeta partition-function free energy exhibits the predicted freezing plateau

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The zeta partition function turns a family of fixed-window values into a normalized free-energy curve; after lower-order subtraction, its reported agreement with beta+1/beta below beta=1 and a plateau near 2 above beta=1 is a numerical freezing diagnostic.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: It identifies the response curve, rather than a single fitted maximum, as the model-discriminating observable and foregrounds that the comparison depends on an externally specified arithmetic renormalization.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after critic revision: the unsupported causal explanation of the plateau was removed, while the qualitative test survives; exact N_T typography and subtraction details require the original PDF.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source defines z_beta(T) by integrating |zeta(1/2+iy)|^(2 beta) over [T,T+2pi], defines normalized f(beta), averages near 10^28, and reports renormalized data consistent with the stated piecewise curve.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: A freezing transition for zeta is not established; domination by a few extremes is only an external heuristic and is not asserted as source fact here.
